senses.gloss: श्नु [śnu], A technical term used by Pāṇini for नु, the sign of the 5th class of roots.
To drip, trickle, fall in drops, distil, drop, ooze or run out, leak out,
Top, surface (in general). (This word has no forms for the first five inflections and is optionally substituted for सानु after acc. dual).
स्नु [snu], f. A sinew, tendon, muscle.
स्नुत [snuta], a. Oozed, dropped, flowed &c.; त्रिष्टुम्मांसात् स्नुतो$नुष्टुब्जगत्यस्थ्नः प्रजापतेः Bhāg.3.12.45.
स्नुषा [snuṣā], A daughter-in-law; समुपास्यत पुत्रभोग्यया स्नुषयेवा- विकृतेन्द्रियः श्रिया R.8.14;15.72.

स्नुह [snuha] स्नुहा [snuhā] हिः [hiḥ], स्नुहा हिः f., -ही The milk-hedge plant. [Raghunandana, the author of Kṛityatattva (Jīvānanda's ed. of Smṛititattva vol. II, 1895) quotes a verse from the Devīpurāṇa in connection with the worship of the goddess Manasā to get rid of the fear of snake-bite (cf. Dr. Kane's History of Dharma-śāstra, vol. V. p. 125). He explains स्नुही as सिजुवृक्षः. The botanic name of the tree is Euphorbia Nerifolia (Mar. निवडुंग). It is a plant from the stem of which a stickly substance oozes out.]
स्नुह् [snuh], 4 P. (स्नुह्यति, स्नुग्ध or स्नूढ) To vomit.
